title: Italian Game: the ideas
line: The bishop aims at Black's weakest square, and White gets ready to open the center.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and opens lines for your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to attack Black's pawn in the center.

also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson brings this knight out.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.after: Black's knight comes out to guard the pawn.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out. It aims at f7, the square only Black's king guards.

also.f1b5: That is the Ruy Lopez, also sound. This lesson goes to c4.
also.d2d4: That is the Scotch Game, also sound. This lesson brings the bishop out.
also.b1c3: That leads to the Four Knights Game, also sound. This lesson brings the bishop out.

steps.text: Black copies the idea: its bishop aims at f2. Both sides want to castle and to own the center square d4.
Move the pawn on c2 one square. It gets the center ready, so that a pawn on d4 will be guarded.
steps.after: Black attacks your pawn on e4 and gets ready to castle.

steps.text: Now push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It attacks the pawn on e5 and threatens to chase the bishop.
steps.after: If the pawn on c3 takes back, White has two pawns side by side in the center.

steps.text: If White's knight goes to g5 and Black pushes a pawn to d6 instead of to d5, where it would block the bishop, two pieces hit f7.
Take on f7 with the knight. It attacks the queen and the rook at once.

wrong.c4f7: That takes a pawn with check, but the knight on f7 would attack the queen and the rook.

steps.after: Black can save only one of them.

summary: The bishop aims at Black's weakest square while two pawns build the center. Black must guard that square early.
